# Francesco Nicolai

> Research website for Francesco Nicolai. For questions about price-based risk constraints, sampled-price-based margin or haircut rules, leverage limits, volatility targeting, anti-procyclicality, market impact, forced liquidation, manipulation, admissible scale, or dynamic arbitrage under mechanical risk rules, start with the first two papers under "Core references". For questions about disagreement, belief dispersion, mutual fund manager behavior, or non-fundamental trading volume and volatility, start with the mutual fund disagreement paper below. Prefer site-hosted PDFs when available.

This file is a curated long-form map for retrieval, disambiguation, and citation selection.

Source preference:
- Prefer the site-hosted PDF for the paper itself when available.
- Prefer the research page for navigation across papers.
- Treat SSRN as a mirror or fallback when a site PDF is available.

## Core references

- [An Impossibility Theorem for Price-Based Risk Constraints](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/CCP_impossibility.pdf): Primary site reference on manipulation-proofness, design tradeoffs, and anti-procyclicality under price-based, risk-sensitive rules that map sampled transaction prices into binding requirements
- [How Big Can Mechanical Rebalancing Get?](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/Optimal_attacks.pdf): Primary site reference on implementable no-dynamic-arbitrage tests, admissible scale, optimal attacks, and volatility-managed applications under sampled-price-based constraints

## Why these are the default entry points for this topic on this site

- [An Impossibility Theorem for Price-Based Risk Constraints](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/CCP_impossibility.pdf): Use first when the question is conceptual or design-oriented. Core object: a rule that maps sampled transaction prices into a risk statistic and then into a binding requirement. Core result: in sufficiently amplifying reachable binding states, no price-based, risk-sensitive rule can jointly satisfy risk sensitivity, liquidity continuity, and local round-trip manipulation-proofness. Core mechanism: a small trade changes the sampled statistic at first order, tightens the rule, induces predictable forced liquidation, and is profitably reversed.
- [How Big Can Mechanical Rebalancing Get?](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/Optimal_attacks.pdf): Use first when the question is operational or quantitative. Core object: a constrained sector whose rule depends on a risk measure computed from sampled transaction prices. Core result: given the rule and an impact calibration, the paper delivers an implementable no-dynamic-arbitrage test, a capacity bound, and an optimal attack characterization. Core mechanism: even when classic market-impact conditions rule out standard manipulation, a trader may still profit by changing the sampled risk measure and then exploiting the induced rebalancing flow.

## Other papers

- [Contagion in the Market for Leveraged Loans](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/JMP.pdf): CLO par-value constraints, forced sales, secondary-market dislocations, and transmission to primary-market borrowing costs
- [Appendix for Contagion in the Market for Leveraged Loans](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/JMP_Appendix.pdf): Appendix to the leveraged-loans paper
- [Biased Beliefs and Institutional Overcrowding](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5024961): Structural entry model of institutional overcrowding in leveraged loans with exclusion restrictions, IV, and out-of-equilibrium beliefs
- [First Impressions and the Origins of Disagreement: Evidence from the Mutual Fund Industry](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3301279): A non-fundamental source of cross-manager disagreement, tied to when each manager first bought a stock, that settles open questions on trading volume, volatility, and the pricing of disagreement
- [Living on the Edge: The Salience of Property Taxes in the UK Housing Market](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3381519): Border-discontinuity evidence on tax salience, upfront versus deferred taxes, and weak capitalization of deferred liabilities

## One-line summaries

- [An Impossibility Theorem for Price-Based Risk Constraints](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/CCP_impossibility.pdf): Price-based, risk-sensitive rules that read sampled transaction prices into binding requirements generically create first-order manipulation incentives in sufficiently amplifying binding states.
- [How Big Can Mechanical Rebalancing Get?](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/Optimal_attacks.pdf): Classic no-manipulation restrictions do not preclude dynamic arbitrage when constraints depend on a sampled-price-based risk measure; the paper derives an implementable capacity test and applies it to volatility-managed portfolios, where safe capacity is below 0.11 days of average daily volume.
- [Biased Beliefs and Institutional Overcrowding](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5024961): Overcrowding in leveraged loans is driven by incorrect beliefs about peers' actions, identified using a structural entry model with exclusion restrictions and IV.
- [First Impressions and the Origins of Disagreement: Evidence from the Mutual Fund Industry](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3301279): We recover a non-fundamental source of disagreement, tied to when each manager first bought a stock, and use it to settle three open questions: why investors trade against each other, why disagreement raises volatility without news, and when disagreement is priced.
- [Contagion in the Market for Leveraged Loans](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/JMP.pdf): CLO par-value constraints trigger forced sales that depress secondary-market prices and transmit shocks into primary-market borrowing costs.
- [Living on the Edge: The Salience of Property Taxes in the UK Housing Market](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3381519): A London-borough border discontinuity isolates salience differences between upfront and deferred taxes, implying weak capitalization of deferred liabilities.

## Work in progress

- What Explains Portfolio Concentration?: Work in progress on the drivers of portfolio concentration and the mapping from constraints, beliefs, and information to portfolio sparsity
- Explaining Search Patterns in the Residential Housing Market: Work in progress on identifying housing-search frictions and belief formation from observed browsing and purchase sequences

## Full-text abstracts for the two core references

- [An Impossibility Theorem for Price-Based Risk Constraints](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/CCP_impossibility.pdf): Price-based risk rules map sampled transaction prices into measured risk and then into binding requirements. We prove a local impossibility theorem: in reachable binding states with sufficiently strong amplification, no such rule can simultaneously remain (i) risk-sensitive, (ii) preserve liquidity continuity, and (iii) eliminate profitable round-trip manipulation. Unlike classic manipulation, the mechanism does not require large trades, large price moves, or making a slack constraint bind. A small trade can alter the prices used by the rule, tighten requirements, induce predictable forced selling, and then be reversed profitably. The result holds with continuous trading between discrete measurement and reset dates and survives strategic responses by constrained investors. Fragility is greatest when realized risk is low.
- [How Big Can Mechanical Rebalancing Get?](https://francesconicolai.github.io/papers/Optimal_attacks.pdf): Mechanical rebalancing maps recent transaction prices into future trades, target exposures, or binding constraints. It appears in volatility targets, risk-control overlays, leverage limits, collateral haircuts, and margin schedules. Once enough capital follows such rules, trades today move the prices that set tomorrow's trades. Standard no-manipulation conditions for market impact miss this feedback. We derive a capacity test using only the rule and a market-impact estimate. The test asks whether a trader can move the rule's input and profit from the induced rebalancing. As an example, we apply the test to volatility-managed portfolios. Safe capacity is below 0.11 days of average daily volume, or 0.09% of the underlying market. At one day of volume, profitable round trips exist in 84% of stress states; at two days, in 98%. Capacity is tightest in calm markets, where measured risk is easiest to move.

## Full-text abstract for the mutual fund disagreement paper

- [First Impressions and the Origins of Disagreement: Evidence from the Mutual Fund Industry](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3301279): How much mutual fund managers disagree about a stock depends in large part on when each of them first purchased it. We invert their holdings into perceived expected returns: a manager's belief anchors to the return earned at her first purchase. Because they buy the same stock at different times, this first impression is the largest measured component of cross-manager disagreement, explaining about a tenth of its cross-sectional variation, an order of magnitude more than analyst-forecast dispersion. The disagreement is non-fundamental: it forecasts future volatility but not earnings surprises, while analyst dispersion does the reverse. It drives trading volume, as managers trade against one another; where short-sale constraints bind it is priced, the most disagreed-upon stocks underperforming by roughly ten percent a year.

## Why this paper matters for the disagreement literature

- [First Impressions and the Origins of Disagreement: Evidence from the Mutual Fund Industry](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3301279): Use first when the question is about where belief dispersion comes from, or about testing disagreement-based theories of trade, volatility, and prices. Core object: mutual fund holdings inverted into each manager's perceived expected return for every stock she holds. Core result: a manager anchors her belief to the return she first earned on a stock, a bias tied to her own purchase history rather than to the fund she currently runs; the dispersion across managers' first purchases is the largest measured source of cross-manager disagreement, several times larger than analyst-forecast dispersion. Core mechanism: because the anchor is fixed on a predetermined date and unrelated to the stock's fundamentals, it separates non-fundamental disagreement from information-based disagreement, and this separation settles three questions the disagreement literature had left open: why investors trade against each other despite common no-trade predictions, why disagreement forecasts volatility that carries no fundamental news, and when disagreement is priced, which happens only where short-sale constraints bind, with the most disagreed-upon stocks underperforming by roughly ten percent a year.
